analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported its Q4 and full-year FY 2025-26 operational and financial performance. The company achieved a record annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity, with a full-year gross refining margin (GRM) of $9.2 per barrel. CPCL is undertaking execution of a Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project of INR 1,600 crores alongside a retail outlet expansion of INR 400 crores over the next 2 to 3 years. Total dividend for the year reached a record INR 62 per share, while net borrowings stood at INR 973 crores. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported a full-year crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for FY 2024-25, representing a 99.5% capacity utilization, and a Q4 throughput of 2.974 MMT at 113% utilization.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects to incur INR 2,000 crores over 2 to 3 years on LOBS and retail projects, along with ~INR 500 crores in normal annual capex.
guidance.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years. Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects a lot of commissioning from its retail outlet expansion during FY 2026-27.
guidance.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

guidance.claim: Management stated there is no M&I in the first 6 months, but a scheduled M&I of one refinery unit is planned close to September or October.
guidance.quote: First, reply to you , in the first 6 months, we don't see any M&I. So it may not be there. But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects maintenance CAPEX to remain around the Rs. 200-250 crore range in the upcoming year.
guidance.quote: The maintenance CAPEX will be at around Rs. 200-250 crore range and depending on value added projects approvals, the actual will be a little different.

guidance.claim: Normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years is expected to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores annually without the LOBS project.
guidance.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL sells close to 90% of its products under long-term agreement to Indian Oil at refinery transfer price (RTP).
demand_outlook.quote: No, our agreement, as you would be aware, close to about 90% of our product, mostly HSD, MS, goes to Indian Oil. We have a tie-up with them, we've a long-term agreement with them for selling. And the agreement is at RTP, that is refinery transfer price.

demand_outlook.claim: There is a shortfall of motor spirit (MS) in the southern market of around 20 TMT per month where production is lower than demand.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Demand growth forecast in the southern market is around 4%-5% for MS and 3% for HSD.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred capex of INR 856 crores in FY26 compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: Execution of the Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project has started in full swing.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The new LOBS project will add 250 KTPA capacity in Group 2 and Group 3 grades.
capex_expansion.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL doubled its Hexane capacity from 30 to 60.
capex_expansion.quote: It was 30, now the capacity is 60.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL spent Rs. 673 crores on CAPEX during FY 2024-25.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores under a 25:75 equity joint venture between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has obtained full physical custody of the 1,200 acres of land required for the new refinery project.
capex_expansion.quote: The most important updates with respect to the project is now we have full custody of the land.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL installed a 1.04 MW capacity ground-mounted and rooftop solar system across its plant area buildings.
capex_expansion.quote: 1.04 MW capacity of Ground Mounted and Roof top solar system on plant area buildings

margins_costs.claim: Q4 FY26 GRM stood at $13.75 per barrel compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: Core GRM for Q4 FY26 was $10.3 per barrel.
Forex loss was approximately INR 200 crores for Q4 and around INR 350 crores for the full year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: Full year GRM for FY 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL recorded a Q4 FY 2024-25 GRM of $6.22 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: Fuel and loss reduced to 8.51% for the full year 2024-25.
margins_costs.quote: and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: Q4 FY 2024-25 inventory gain was $0.66 per barrel or Rs. 125 crores, whereas full-year inventory loss was $0.06 per barrel or Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only. But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a GRM of $3.40 per barrel for 9M FY 2024-25 compared to $8.64 per barrel in FY 2023-24.
Core Gross Refining Margin stood at $3.75 per barrel in 9M FY 2024-25 compared to $8.21 per barrel in FY 2023-24.
Net operating expenditure for 9M FY 2024-25 was ₹945 crore.
Singapore GRM was reported at $4.02 per barrel for 9M FY 2024-25 compared to $6.58 per barrel in FY 2023-24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a record annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: Q4 FY26 crude throughput reached 2.93 MMT, equivalent to 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a record distillate yield of 79.1% during the financial year.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: Annual diesel production reached 5.139 MMT and petrol production reached 1.318 MMT.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: Full-year crude throughput stood at 10.45 MMT, representing 99.5% capacity utilization, while Q4 crude throughput reached 2.974 MMT or 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year and if you take that into consideration , you will find that this performance is quite comparable to the previous year's performance where CPCL clocked 111% capacity utilization and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: RLNG consumption increased to 527 TMT in FY 2024-25 from 441 TMT in the prior year.
orders_capacity.quote: With respect to RLNG and our commitment to net zero, RLNG consumption during the year FY 2024-25, was 527 TMT as against 441 TMT in the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: Manali Refinery has an installed capacity of 10.5 MMTPA.
Crude throughput reached 7,480 TMT in 9M FY 2024-25 compared to 11,642 TMT in FY 2023-24.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL reported gross borrowings of INR 1,900 crores and net borrowings of INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share in addition to an interim dividend of INR 8 per share, totaling INR 62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: Debt to equity ratio stood at 0.39 as of March 31, 2025, with total debt at Rs. 3,100 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year. At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's net worth stood at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share (50% of face value) for FY 2024-25.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL recorded net worth of ₹7,491 crore as of 9M FY 2024-25.
CPCL's working capital stood at ₹5,098 crore as on 31.03.2024 compared to ₹2,467 crore as on 31.03.2023.

risks_headwinds.claim: Logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility present ongoing operational challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Short-term supply disruptions affected 30% to 40% of Middle East crude supply over a brief period.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Maintenance and inspection shutdowns lead to startup and shutdown costs that keep operating costs temporarily elevated.
risks_headwinds.quote: Plus, every M&I shutdown also involves startup and shutdown cost. So, the operating cost also remains little elevated.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL recorded exchange variation loss of ₹122 crore for 9M FY 2024-25.
CST under recovery was ₹246 crore for 9M FY 2024-25.
Provision for contingent liabilities was ₹9 crore for 9M FY 2024-25.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects commissioning out of its retail outlet project with 300 licenses in FY 2026-27.
management_commitments.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL plans to incur INR 2,000 crores across its LOBS and retail outlet projects over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Normal maintenance CAPEX is expected to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores annually over the next two years.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
